fivewhychain.title: Root cause: the SMB churn spike
fivewhychain.problem: SMB churn nearly doubled in two months

whys.question: Why did SMB churn spike?
whys.answer: 58% of cancellations cite the February price increase.

whys.question: Why did the price increase hit so hard?
whys.answer: It landed as a flat 40% jump with no advance notice.

whys.question: Why no advance notice or phased rollout?
whys.answer: The pricing change shipped with the Q1 close, not a customer-comms plan.

whys.question: Why wasn't comms part of the pricing rollout?
whys.answer: Pricing changes have never needed sign-off from anyone outside finance.

whys.question: Why is there no cross-team sign-off on pricing?
whys.answer: There's no defined process connecting pricing, growth, and support before a change ships.

fivewhychain.rootCause: Missing cross-team process for pricing changes, not the price itself.
fivewhychain.footer: Fix the process and the next price change stops costing accounts.

argumentmap.title: SN2 vs SN1, which mechanism?
argumentmap.claim: The reaction proceeds via an SN2 (bimolecular nucleophilic substitution) mechanism.

premises.text: Primary substrate, minimal steric hindrance favors backside attack.
Strong nucleophile (OH⁻) present in high concentration.
Rate is second-order: rate = k[CH₃Br][OH⁻], both species appear in rate law.
Polar protic solvent (water) could stabilise a carbocation and favour SN1.
Solvent choice matters: aprotic solvents would further favour SN2 by not solvating the nucleophile.

argumentmap.verdict: SN2 dominates: primary substrate + strong nucleophile + second-order kinetics all point the same way.

algorithmtrace.title: Bubble Sort — First Pass

steps.caption: Start the pass: compare the first adjacent pair, 5 and 1.
5 > 1, so swap them — the larger value bubbles right.
Advance the window and compare 5 and 4.
Compare 5 and 8 — already in order, no swap.
The largest value, 8, settles into the last sorted slot.

algorithmtrace.caption: Step through one full pass: each comparison either holds or swaps, walking the largest remaining value to the right end.
algorithmtrace.footer: After this pass the maximum (8) is locked in its final position; bubble sort repeats over the shrinking unsorted prefix.

dptable.title: LCS — Longest Common Subsequence: "ABCB" vs "BCAB"
dptable.recurrence: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1]+1 if s[i]=t[j], else max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1])

steps.caption: Base case: row 0 and col 0 are all 0 — empty string has LCS 0 with anything.
dp[1][3]: A matches A → dp[0][2]+1 = 1. First character matched.
dp[2][4]: B matches B → dp[1][3]+1 = 2. Two-character match.
dp[4][4]: B matches B → dp[3][3]+1 = 3. Final answer: LCS = "BCB" (length 3).

dptable.footer: LCS is "BCB" (length 3). Backtrack from dp[4][4]=3 via diagonal match cells. Classic FAANG problem: edit distance, diff tools, DNA sequencing.

cyclewheel.title: The water cycle
cyclewheel.caption: A closed loop driven by the sun: water leaves the surface as vapor, returns as precipitation, and collects to start the round again.
cyclewheel.footer: No water is created or lost — the same supply circulates endlessly between the surface, the atmosphere, and back.

hashtable.title: Hash table — separate chaining, h(k) = k mod 7
hashtable.footer: Keys 7, 14 and 21 hash to bucket 0 (all divisible by 7). Key 10 hashes to bucket 3, colliding with key 3 — the chain is walked to find Eve. Load factor = 6/7 ≈ 86%.

trie.title: Prefix tree (Trie) — autocomplete words
trie.footer: Trie lookup: O(m) where m = word length, regardless of dictionary size. Each edge is one character; double-ringed nodes mark end-of-word. Use for autocomplete, spell-check, prefix search.

graphtrace.title: BFS Graph Traversal

steps.caption: Start BFS at A. Add A to queue.
Dequeue A. Enqueue neighbors B and C.
Dequeue B. Enqueue neighbors D and E.
Dequeue F. Queue empty — BFS complete! Order: A B C D E F.

graphtrace.footer: BFS visits nodes level-by-level (breadth-first). Queue is FIFO. Time: O(V+E). Contrast with DFS which uses a stack and goes deep before wide.

binarytree.title: BST Search — find 7
binarytree.footer: BST search: O(h) time where h is tree height — O(log n) balanced, O(n) worst case. Each comparison halves the search space in a balanced BST.

sortingviz.title: Bubble Sort step-by-step
sortingviz.footer: Bubble sort: O(n²) time. Each pass bubbles the largest unsorted element to its final position. Simple to understand, rarely used in practice.

gridtrace.title: BFS Shortest Path on a Grid

steps.caption: Find shortest path S→E. Walls (#) block movement.
BFS expands: S visited, neighbors queued.
Wave reaches E. Shortest path length = 5.

gridtrace.footer: BFS guarantees shortest path in unweighted grids. O(rows×cols). Classic FAANG: islands (LC 200), rotting oranges (994), word search (79).
